paper text.text:
In (a), the unique bridge $B$ lies in a facial disk $F$ whose boundary
contains $a,b,c,d$. With the exception of $abcd$, every attachment
sequence of such a face of $\Psi_1/s_3t_3$ also occurs for $\Psi_1$,
up to cyclic shift and reversal~\supp{R2}. When the sequences agree,
a homeomorphism of the two disks matching the boundary appearances
carries the drawing of $B$ to the corresponding face of $\Psi_1$.

In (b), the bridge uses only $a,b,c$. Omitting $d$ from the
facial walks gives the same sequences containing $a,b,c$ for
$\Psi_1/s_3t_3$ and $\Psi_1$, up to cyclic shift and reversal~\supp{R2}.
Thus the bridge can be drawn in the corresponding face of $\Psi_1$.

The regions along $P_1$ in the two graphs are compared in~\supp{R2}.
If the region is an annulus, its boundary sequences are $ac\mid b$,
$ac\mid bd$, $a\mid b$ or $a\mid bd$. All four occur for $\Psi_1$, so
Lemma~\ref{lem:annulus-embedding} gives a torus embedding of $H$.

If the region is a disk, its sequence is $ab$, $abc$, $abd$, $abcd$
or $acdbdc$. The sequences $ab$ and $acdbdc$ also occur for $\Psi_1$.
In the disk with sequence $acdbdc$, the appearances after $b$ give
either $abc$ or $abd$ by using just $c$ or just $d$. Thus only $abcd$
with all four attachments remains.

what: Every rotation system of Psi_1/s3t3, with P_1, P_2 the edges ab, cd (a = s1, b = t1, c = s2, d = t2) and the edge s3t3 contracted into s3. Attachments a, b, c, d; twins and s3 omitted.
how to read: At each vertex, 'cyclic orders' lists the neighbor orders lexicographically, starting each order with the least neighbor. Rotation systems are numbered from 0 in the order of 'vertices', with the last vertex varying fastest. The entry rows[i] indexes 'distinct rows' for rotation system i. Each row gives the genus (2 - V + E - F)/2 and the sorted attachment sequences of the facial walks. After u->v a walk takes v->w, where w follows u at v. A sequence records every visit to an attachment, starting at the least cyclic shift and keeping the walk direction. For claims up to reversal, take the least cyclic shift of either direction.

graphs.name: Psi_1/s3t3 (a = s1, b = t1, c = s2, d = t2; the edge s3t3 contracted into s3)
graphs.row format: [genus, attachment sequences of the facial walks, for a torus rotation the region along P_1 = ab (the faces on the two sides of ab glued along it: a disk, or an annulus when the same face lies on both sides), up to cyclic shift and reversal]

claims.statement: Psi_1/s3t3 is connected and nonplanar, so its torus embeddings are cellular.

Comparison with Psi_1 (the table R1, with a = s1, b = t1, c = s2, d = t2): the faces meeting at least three of a, b, c, d and the regions glued along P_1 = ab, over all torus rotations, up to cyclic shift and reversal, with the number of torus rotations in which each occurs.
The only new disk attachment sequences are a,b,c,d and three-vertex orders that, up to reversal, are restrictions of a,b,d,c; no new annulus occurs.
In (a) and (b), a simple face of Psi_1 has order a,b,d,c.
In (c), gluing the two simple facial disks of Psi_1 along P_1 gives a disk with attachment sequence a,c,d,b,d,c.
